exhibits.name: Tension / integrity
exhibits.subtitle: Thirty struts. One continuous network.
exhibits.description: Separate compression members are held within a connected network of tension. Thirty struts and ninety cables make a sphere with no strut-to-strut contacts.
exhibits.credit: Fuller’s tensegrity explorations · Kenneth Snelson’s foundational contribution
exhibits.note: Independent icosahedral construction. The assembled geometry admits positive cable self-stress; this is not a loaded structural analysis. The motion is geometric: cables change length, while struts remain rigid.

exhibits.name: A house that hangs
exhibits.subtitle: Dymaxion / Wichita House
exhibits.description: A lightweight circular house suspended from a central mast. A band of windows sits between the aluminium skirt and its gently domed, segmented roof.
exhibits.note: Overall diameter 36 ft and height 22 ft follow the Docomomo record. Roof curvature, window divisions and fit-out are estimated from museum photographs. Forty-eight roof gores and twenty-four floor spokes simplify the original construction.

exhibits.name: A climate of ideas
exhibits.subtitle: Montréal Biosphère
exhibits.description: An almost complete sphere of open lattice, wrapping a separate building inside. The modern, unclad structure is shown here as a study of enclosure without a wall.
exhibits.note: Nominal 76 m diameter and 62 m height are working published dimensions. A coarser six-frequency geodesic grid and simplified inner lattice represent the space frame; neither the node pattern nor the internal building is an as-built reconstruction.

exhibits.name: Living in the experiment
exhibits.subtitle: The Fuller dome home / Carbondale
exhibits.description: Bucky and Anne’s own home brought the geodesic idea down to domestic scale. Pale triangular roof panels meet five blue entrance and window bays.
exhibits.credit: R. Buckminster Fuller & Anne Hewlett Fuller · Pease prefabrication
exhibits.note: A three-frequency icosahedral cap with five clipped bays follows the visible composition. Approximate 39 ft 1 in diameter and 16 ft 6 in height follow the restoration architect’s account; bay cuts and windows are estimated.

form.method: Independent icosahedral edge rotation construction. Positive cable force densities and negative strut density solved for unloaded nominal geometry. Does not certify stability, loads or the animation path.
